name: Cytron MD10C 13 A DC motor driver
description: Cytron MD10C R3.0 single-channel brushed DC motor driver: a full NMOS H-bridge running one motor forwards, backwards or braked from two logic inputs (PWM for speed up to 20 kHz, DIR for direction; 3.3 V or 5 V logic), motor supply 5-30 V, 13 A continuous, 30 A peak for 10 s. Powered from the motor supply only (no logic supply pin), no reverse-polarity protection, test buttons and A/B direction LEDs on board. Sold as: Cytron MD10C R3.0 10Amp 5V-30V DC Motor Driver, 3-pin control header (1 GND, 2 PWM, 3 DIR) plus a POWER screw terminal (1 +, 2 -) and a MOTOR screw terminal (3 A, 4 B) on the opposite edge.
eli5: A strong switch box that lets your board run one big DC motor forwards or backwards at any speed, using a separate battery for the motor.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Control header pin 1: logic ground; connect to the microcontroller GND (common with the motor supply -)

pins.name: PWM
pins.description: Control header pin 2: speed input. High = drive, low = brake (both outputs low). PWM up to 20 kHz; logic high 3-5.5 V, low 0-0.5 V. Not for RC-receiver servo pulses

pins.name: DIR
pins.description: Control header pin 3: direction input. Low = forward (output A high, B low), high = reverse (A low, B high); logic high 3-5.5 V

pins.name: POWER+
pins.description: POWER screw terminal 1: motor supply + (5-30 V DC) from a battery/PSU able to supply the motor current. Also powers the board. NO reverse-polarity protection. Never connect to the microcontroller

pins.name: MOTOR_A
pins.description: MOTOR screw terminal 3: motor output A; connect the motor, never the microcontroller

pins.name: MOTOR_B
pins.description: MOTOR screw terminal 4: motor output B

supplierQuery: Cytron MD10C R3 10A DC motor driver
buildNotes: Truth table (Cytron MD10C R3.0 user's manual, 3G): PWM low = brake (A and B low); PWM high + DIR low = forward (A high, B low); PWM high + DIR high = reverse (A low, B high). There is no coast state.
Sign-magnitude control: PWM duty on the PWM pin sets speed, DIR sets direction. Locked-antiphase also works: hold PWM high and feed the PWM signal to DIR (50 % duty = stop).
Motor supply 5-30 V DC into the POWER terminal; the board needs no other supply. Check polarity: there is no reverse-polarity protection.
Join the control header GND to the microcontroller GND.
Logic inputs: high 3-5.5 V, low 0-0.5 V, so 3.3 V GPIOs (ESP32, Pico) drive them directly.
PWM frequency at most 20 kHz; the output switches at the input frequency. Use a microcontroller PWM, not an RC receiver.
13 A continuous (25 C, no heatsink or airflow), 30 A peak for at most 10 s. Use thick wires and a fuse sized for the motor.

driver.code:
# Cytron MD10C R3.0 13 A DC motor driver, MicroPython driver.
# One H-bridge (4 NMOS), one brushed DC motor, powered from the motor supply only (5-30 V).
# Control header (Cytron MD10C R3.0 user's manual, section 3G): 1 GND, 2 PWM, 3 DIR.
# Truth table (same section):
#   PWM = 0, DIR = X -> A low,  B low : brake (low-side)
#   PWM = 1, DIR = 0 -> A high, B low : forward (current A -> B)
#   PWM = 1, DIR = 1 -> A low,  B high: reverse (current B -> A)
# Sign-magnitude PWM: PWM pin carries the speed duty, DIR selects the direction.
# The off part of each PWM period brakes (slow decay), so speed is roughly proportional to duty.
# PWM frequency at most 20 kHz (output frequency = input frequency); 10 kHz default.
# Inputs: high 3-5.5 V, low 0-0.5 V, so 3.3 V GPIOs drive them directly.
# (Locked-antiphase mode, PWM held high and the PWM signal on DIR with 50 % = stop, is also supported by the
#  board; this driver uses sign-magnitude.)
from machine import Pin, PWM

MAX_FREQ = 20000


class MD10C:
    def __init__(self, pwm, dir, freq=10000):
        """pwm, dir: GPIO numbers wired to the PWM and DIR header pins. freq: PWM frequency, <= 20 kHz."""
        if freq > MAX_FREQ:
            raise ValueError('MD10C PWM frequency must be <= 20 kHz')
        self.dir = Pin(dir, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.pwm = PWM(Pin(pwm), freq=freq, duty_u16=0)

    @staticmethod
    def _duty(speed):
        speed = max(0, min(100, speed))
        return speed * 65535 // 100

    def forward(self, speed=100):
        """DIR low, PWM = speed %: output A high, B low while PWM is high."""
        self.pwm.duty_u16(0)
        self.dir.value(0)
        self.pwm.duty_u16(self._duty(speed))

    def reverse(self, speed=100):
        """DIR high, PWM = speed %: output A low, B high while PWM is high."""
        self.pwm.duty_u16(0)
        self.dir.value(1)
        self.pwm.duty_u16(self._duty(speed))

    def drive(self, speed):
        """speed -100..100: positive = forward, negative = reverse, 0 = brake."""
        if speed > 0:
            self.forward(speed)
        elif speed < 0:
            self.reverse(-speed)
        else:
            self.brake()

    def brake(self):
        """PWM low: both outputs low, the motor is shorted and stops quickly. (The MD10C has no coast state.)"""
        self.pwm.duty_u16(0)

    def stop(self):
        self.brake()

example.code:
import time
from md10c import MD10C

motor = MD10C({PWM}, {DIR})
while True:
    motor.forward(100)
    print('forward')
    time.sleep(1)
    motor.brake()
    print('brake')
    time.sleep(1)
    motor.reverse(100)
    print('reverse')
    time.sleep(1)
    motor.brake()
    print('brake')
    time.sleep(1)
